sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Identify the following methods of transferring designs with their descriptions: (i) Uses a glass plate and light to trace the design directly onto the fabric (ii) Involves tracing the design on butter paper and making small holes along it (iii) Drawing the design directly on the fabric with a pencil (iv) Uses carbon paper to transfer the design onto the fabric.
questions.answer: (i) Glass plate and light method. (ii) Butter paper (perforated pattern) method. (iii) Direct method. (iv) Carbon paper method.

questions.q: State True or False. (a) A motif repeated over a surface gives a pattern. (b) Dark fabric needs blue carbon paper.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: white or yellow carbon is used on dark fabric.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Geometrical design (b) Abstract design. B: (i) Made of lines and shapes (ii) No specific inspiration (iii) Close to nature.
Rearrange the letters: (a) EPATELMT (b) BTCAINGCRKA.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of enlarging or reducing a design?
questions.answer: It lets one motif be used on articles of different sizes and shapes. The design size can then fit the size of the article.

questions.q: How will you change a small design into a large design?
questions.answer: Trace the design, transfer it with carbon paper on graph paper and draw it on larger squares. Each part is enlarged equally in width and height.

questions.q: Compare a geometrical design with an abstract design.
questions.answer: A geometrical design is built from lines and shapes like circles and squares. An abstract design has no specific inspiration and uses only texture, veins or colour of an object.

questions.q: What four factors will you consider while selecting an embroidery design for a baby's frock?
questions.answer: The age of the baby so decorations like stones or zari that scratch should be avoided. Soft light fabric, comfort, safe thread and a simple naturalized or simplified design (and bright colours).

questions.q: Give two comparisons between stylised and geometrical design.
questions.answer: Stylised designs have more curves and details and are away from natural form; geometrical designs use simple shapes and straight lines. Stylised designs look decorative and complicated while geometrical ones look simple.

questions.q: Differentiate between a motif and a pattern.
questions.answer: A motif is the basic unit of a design. A pattern is made by repeating the motif at intervals.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any two methods of transferring a design from paper onto fabric.
questions.answer: (i) Carbon paper: place carbon face down between fabric and design and trace with a dry ball pen. (ii) Back tracing: go over the back of the lines of a tracing with a 2B pencil, tape it to the fabric and trace the lines with the back of a pencil.

questions.q: List the factors to consider while selecting a design for a frock for a three-year-old niece (three points).
questions.answer: (i) It should suit her age: soft fabric, light embroidery and no stones or zari that scratch. (ii) Simple naturalized or cartoon designs in bright colours with safe threads. (iii) The size should suit the frock and embroidery should be at points of emphasis.

questions.q: Explain the five types of designs briefly.
questions.answer: (i) Geometrical designs use shapes and lines and simplified designs use slight curves with few details. (ii) Naturalized designs are close to nature. (iii) Stylised designs are decorative with more curves; abstract designs have no specific inspiration.

questions.q: Explain the factors to be considered while planning an eco-friendly shopping bag.
questions.answer: (i) It must be light but strong with strong handles. (ii) The fabric must be water resistant, colour fast and non-absorbent such as canvas or jute. (iii) The embroidery must not snag and should suit all age groups.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the six methods of transferring a design on a fabric.
questions.answer: (i) Direct method: freehand pencil on thin fabrics like georgette. (ii) Carbon paper: trace with a dry ball pen, using white carbon on dark fabric. (iii) Back tracing: pencil the back of a tracing and trace over it. (iv) Butter paper: prick holes along the lines and rub with a paste of blue powder in kerosene. (v) Glass plate and light: outline with a hard pencil over a bulb under glass. (vi) Template: card paper shape traced for repeated simple designs.
